video.title: NavigationStack, NavigationLink & Navigation Path | Day 141
video.description:
Learn to explain how to move between screens in SwiftUI: NavigationStack, NavigationLink & Navigation Path, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
NavigationStack - A container that lets the user move forward through screens and go back.
NavigationLink - A view that the user taps to go to another screen.
Navigation Path - A list of values that stores which screens are on the stack.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: SwiftUI NavigationStack, NavigationLink & Navigation Path | Day 141
landscape.description:
Explain NavigationStack, NavigationLink & Navigation Path in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
내비게이션스택, 내비게이션링크, 내비게이션 패스 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

NavigationStack - A container that lets the user move forward through screens and go back.
한국어: 내비게이션스택: 사용자가 화면을 앞으로 이동하고 뒤로 돌아오게 하는 컨테이너

NavigationLink - A view that the user taps to go to another screen.
한국어: 내비게이션링크: 사용자가 탭하면 다른 화면으로 이동하는 뷰

Navigation Path - A list of values that stores which screens are on the stack.
한국어: 내비게이션 패스: 스택에 어떤 화면이 쌓여 있는지 저장하는 값의 목록

In this video, Mina and Jake add a second screen to an app, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain NavigationStack, NavigationLink and Navigation Path in English?

dialogue.title: A second screen

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I need a second screen in my app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrap the first screen in a NavigationStack. It lets the user move forward and go back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does the user go to the next screen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a NavigationLink. The user taps it, and the next screen slides in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I added a NavigationLink without a NavigationStack, and it did nothing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A NavigationLink only works inside a NavigationStack.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now I want to open a screen from code, not from a tap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a Navigation Path. It stores the values for the screens on the stack.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I push a screen with it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Append a value to the Navigation Path, like `path.append` in the code. The stack shows it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Remove the last value from the Navigation Path. The stack goes back one screen.
Wrap the screen in a NavigationStack.
